faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour is for permanent employees. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum rate $33.05 per hour. Super is paid on top of the base rate.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy of 2% also applies. Use the tax-free threshold if eligible.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia

When you're offered a job or negotiating a pay rise, you might wonder how your hourly rate stacks up as an annual salary. In Australia, the standard conversion uses a 38-hour week, but many people work different hours. This guide explains the formula, the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax – and we'll touch on what is the minimum wage in America for comparison.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The simplest way to estimate your annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a full-time employee, the typical assumption is 38 hours per week. For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

If you work part-time, use your actual weekly hours. The formula works for any schedule – just multiply by 52 to get the yearly figure.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This rate is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most workers are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. Award rates vary by classification and often include penalty rates for weekends, nights, or public holidays.

It's important to check your specific award – you can find pay guides on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on our site has more details.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, this means casuals earn $33.05 per hour. When using our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, you can tick a box to add casual loading – never type a rate that already includes loading.

Superannuation (super) is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost to the employer. So if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer contributes an extra $7,200 to your super fund.

### Fortnightly Pay and Tax

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For example, a $30/hour rate with 38 hours gives $1,140 per week, or $2,280 per fortnight.

Tax is withheld by your employer using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2%. The tax-free threshold is included if you're a resident. Note that HELP debts, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not accounted for in our estimates.

### What is the Minimum Wage in America?

For context, what is the minimum wage in America? The US federal minimum wage is $7.25 per hour, though many states and cities have higher rates. Unlike Australia, the US does not have a universal superannuation system, and casual loading is not standard. When comparing, remember that Australian wages include compulsory super and often higher award rates. The Australian National Minimum Wage of $26.44 is significantly higher than the US federal rate, but cost of living and social benefits differ.

### Average Weekly Earnings and Your Pay

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for a specific job. Your pay may be higher or lower depending on your industry, experience, and location.

### Important Disclaimer

Our annual pay estimate uses the formula hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed calculations, check our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page or the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide.
